transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Novarise ML), Sofia (Novarise Platform), Ethan (Novarise CTO)

Summary (auto): quick mid-poc sync to compare throughput/latency against incumbent (CloudServe). Went over sprint 2 numbers, saw throughput headroom but tail-latency spikes at 95th pct under burst. Discussed routing rules, quantization profile, and KV cache priming. Agreed next steps around dedicated slot request and extended head-to-head load run.

00:00 Marcus: ok hey everyone thanks for joining on a Friday, real quick agenda - sprint 2 numbers, tuned runs we did last night, and then decision points for next week
00:18 Daniel: yeah thanks Marcus, sorry running late, had a standup overrun so i'll be brief, curious about the 95th pct spikes you mentioned in email
00:36 Priya: hi all, i'll run through the runs - quick note, last night we pushed quantize v2 and reduced fp16 fallback, so nominal token cost dropped but we saw some tail noise when concurrency hit >80
01:05 Sofia: can you remind me what model variant you used for that run? we were testing against CloudServe's prod endpoint with their L2 quantize, right?
01:18 Priya: correct - we used redwood-gpt-large-q2 (note: naming in transcript may be off) guess we should call it q2 for the meeting. Baseline was CloudServe-curie-ish endpoint (they sent a trimmed config)
01:42 Marcus: high level: median latency improved ~14% vs baseline on same token mix, throughput (tokens/sec) improved ~22% on our dedicated slot config; but 95th went up ~8% in bursts — likely KV priming + context switching under bursty concurrency
02:10 Ethan: ok 14% median is nice but our SLA is really about 99th and user-perceived latency. that 95th bump worries me, any mitigation ideas?
02:29 Priya: yep so we dug in - two patterns: first, cold KV cache on novel prefixes cause long tail. second, occasional GPU kernel fallback to slower exec path when sequence length jumps beyond our tuned kernel window
02:53 Daniel: that second one, do you mean the kernel selector chose a generic kernel and that slowed things? is that deterministic?
03:07 Priya: more or less yes, selector heuristics pick optimized kernels for common sequence lengths, when a request has unusual length we fall back. we've got a couple of mitigations - widen kernel window and pre-sample the seq length distribution, and also warm the KV cache by synthetic prefetching for top 200 prefixes
03:36 Marcus: we did a controlled run last night with warm-KV and widened kernel window — that recovered most of the 95th; numbers in the spreadsheet I uploaded in the deck
03:50 Sofia: can you repost that deck link? my email thread lost the inline spreadsheet
04:00 Marcus: sure posting in chat now: https://redwood-docs/internal/poc/novarise-sprint2-runbook (note: link is internal placeholder)
04:20 Priya: also worth noting our batching policy: we previously used continuous batching aggressive mode which gave best throughput but adds jitter for single-request tail. for apps where 95th/99th matters you can lower batching delay and sacrifice ~6-8% throughput
04:48 Daniel: hmm yeah we need predictability for call routing decisions. throughput win is good for cost, but for user workflows we'd rather be consistent
05:06 Marcus: decision point: do you want us to prioritize median/throughput (cost) or tail predictability for next sprint?
05:19 Ethan: leaning tail predictability, but willing to compromise if the cost delta is under 15%
05:32 Priya: pragmatic approach: enable KV warm-up for high-frequency prefixes + conservative batching for Alpha routing, keep aggressive batching for background jobs. also add a fallback route to CloudServe for heavy tails as a safety net
05:56 Daniel: fallback to CloudServe — won't that complicate auditing and data residency? we have to keep logs audited and not leak PII to third parties
06:15 Marcus: yes that's why we framed fallback as "model variant in-region" not cross-tenant — fallback would still be under our dedicated, or we can fallback to your committed CloudServe private instance if you have that contract. also we can attach RBAC and retention policies to log exports
06:42 Sofia: speaking of security, can you double-check KMS flow? last week compliance flagged a question about envelope encryption when streaming to external fallback
06:58 Priya: yeah quick explanation — we use customer-managed keys for private deployments, envelope rotates every 24 hours; when invoking fallback to third party you'd need explicit key escrow / contractual terms. i'll add a security note in the write-up
07:20 Marcus: noted. next step: i'll add a KMS section to the doc and include key-flow diagrams
07:34 Daniel: back to numbers, can you call out exact test scenario - was the workload mixed-short/long prompts or mostly long?
07:45 Priya: it was 65% short (<64 tokens), 30% mid (64-256), 5% long (>256). the long ones drove the kernel fallback we saw
08:05 Marcus: and baseline's mix? they simulated 70% short, 25% mid, 5% long — fairly close but their sequencing had fewer abrupt length jumps, that helped their tail
08:22 Sofia: ok makes sense. what's the recommendation for quantization profile? earlier you mentioned v2 - are there tradeoffs to push to v3 now?
08:34 Priya: v3 would be more aggressive int8 sparsity and reduce cost another 10-12% but might increase instability on certain ops; we prefer staged rollout: run v3 on background workloads first, then a small canary set of production queries
08:52 Ethan: do we have a canary plan that doesn't impact users if it degrades?
09:01 Marcus: yes, Redwood's rollout supports canary percentages and automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency SLO breaches. we can set the threshold to 0.5% initially
09:14 Daniel: quality regression checks — are those textual evals or do you run similarity scores?
09:22 Priya: both — we run perplexity surrogate checks and also embed+similarity for semantics; for your domain we also wire up a prompt set of 200 critical flows we've been using for evals
09:38 Sofia: small nit — in the logs i saw references to "K-V cash" sometimes, transcription error?
09:46 Priya: heh, yeah human transcripts sometimes mess up KV-caching to K-V cash, noted
09:52 Marcus: ok moving to the head-to-head numbers in the sheet, i'll read the important bits: baseline median 92ms / 95th 210ms, our median 79ms / 95th 227ms in aggressive mode; with warm-KV + conservative batching our 95th dropped to 198ms and median 85ms
10:28 Daniel: so with mitigations you're below baseline on 95th, median slightly worse than earlier but still better than baseline's median?
10:39 Priya: correct — the warm-KV run gave us the best balance, throughput was ~18% higher than baseline and unit token cost estimated ~12% lower (based on current infra pricing)
11:00 Ethan: curious about noise on the 99th — do you have 99th numbers?
11:08 Priya: 99th is noisy but on the warm-KV run we saw 99th ~330ms vs baseline 360ms — so still an improvement but with wider variance on rare tails
11:25 Marcus: full raw logs and aggregated percentiles are in the spreadsheet; we'll share the link after the call
11:31 Sofia: thanks, please include raw traces for a few outlier requests so our infra team can look at call stacks
11:42 Priya: will do, i'll attach a few goroutine traces and GPU kernel logs (again anonymized)
12:00 Marcus: question from our side — do you want us to provision a dedicated 4-GPU slot for the rest of the pilot so you can see steady-state numbers?
12:14 Daniel: cost question — what's the delta monthly for a dedicated 4-GPU vs shared?
12:22 Marcus: rough math: dedicated 4xA100-equivalent about 3x the unit cost of our shared slots but gives much lower variance. i'll include exact numbers in pricing sheet for decision
12:36 Ethan: can you also include preemptible vs reserved pricing and an option for peak-burst reserved with autoscaling? we'd like to weigh commitment vs. flexibility
12:46 Marcus: yep will include those options
12:52 Priya: while we're on architecture, wanted to highlight routing rules we tested: route by latency SLO (fast-path) and cost SLO (economy-path), with automated fallback to the economy-path when queue length hits threshold. That gave predictable throughput but introduced a few misrouted requests in the tail case we saw
13:15 Daniel: would you recommend sticky routing by user session? i.e. keep a given user on the same route to preserve warm-KV
13:25 Priya: session-stickiness helps a lot for KV hot prefixes, but has tradeoffs for load balancing. hybrid approach: sticky for top-5% heavy users and round-robin for the rest
13:39 Sofia: ok makes sense. operationally can we expose route-level metrics to our SRE?
13:47 Marcus: yes, console supports per-route dashboards, token-level cost, and trace links. we can grant SRE read-only access scoped to the pilot project
14:05 Ethan: compliance again — audit logs, can we get 13 months retention and export to your S3 or our vault?
14:18 Marcus: default is 90 days but enterprise addon supports 13 months and export hooks to your S3 with SSE-C or to your vault via API; i'll put the options in the security doc
14:36 Daniel: switching gears, any notable anomalies in the runs?
14:44 Priya: one anomaly - around 30:12 in the run we had a host level swap that caused a 1.2s outlier; that was due to GPU driver noise on our test cluster — we've flagged it and excluded that trace from the aggregate numbers for fairness
15:00 Sofia: good call. also we noticed the baseline had a larger container lifetime churn which sometimes reduced their tail, weirdly
15:12 Priya: sometimes churn reduces queuing but increases cold-starts; it's a weird tradeoff
15:22 Marcus: ok near the end here - decisions: Novarise wants tail predictability prioritized, wants a dedicated 4-GPU trial, and needs security & KMS diagrams. Any objections?
15:35 Ethan: sounds right, pending the delta on committed pricing
15:45 Daniel: we'll authorize the extended run once we see the committed pricing and the EV for stability looks good
15:56 Marcus: great we'll send the pricing and slot request by Monday 5/15; Priya will send the kernel logs and quant profile by Wed 5/17
16:10 Sofia: and we'll run the second head-to-head load and share results by 5/20, we'll also loop in procurement if the delta is reasonable
16:28 Marcus: cool, last quick Q - do you want the fallback plan documented as automatic fallback or manual failover?
16:40 Ethan: automatic for critical flows, manual for non-critical; call that out in the runbook please
16:52 Priya: noted — automatic fallback limited to in-region variants, manual for cross-region fallbacks
17:05 Marcus: thanks team, we'll follow up with artifacts. end of call.

Attachments referenced: pricing-sheet-v2.xlsx (uploaded to deck), warm-kv-run-logs.tar.gz (link in deck), quantize-profiles-v2-v3-notes.md

Transcript notes: occasional speaker attribution issues (Priya sometimes labeled Speaker 2), transcription has some homophone errors (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), timestamps approximate.
